civil_disposition.basis: Civil cases closed in the fiscal year (IDB termination records), grouped by how each case ended, using the disposition codes in the FJC civil codebook.
civil_disposition.definitions: Settled means the case was dismissed after the parties settled out of court. A case withdrawn by the plaintiff is a voluntary dismissal. Other dismissals include want of prosecution and lack of jurisdiction. Judgments on a motion before trial include orders dismissing prisoner petitions. Jury trials include directed verdicts. Other judgments include arbitration awards, stays for bankruptcy and judgments the court coded as other. Transferred or remanded covers transfers to another district or to a multidistrict litigation court, and remands to state court or a federal agency. A statistical closing ends a case open more than three years with no activity for a year.
civil_disposition.formula: share = 100 × civil cases closed this way ÷ all civil cases closed in the district that year, rounded to 1 decimal

groups.label: Judgment on a motion before trial
Judgment on a motion before trial

national_note.text: 147,231 of the 407,539 civil cases closed in all districts in FY 2025 were part of MDL 2885 in N.D. Fla., one multidistrict litigation docket. The all-district shares for that year include them.

civil_nature_of_suit.basis: Civil cases filed in the fiscal year (IDB filing cohort), grouped by the nature-of-suit categories on the AO civil cover sheet (JS 44).
civil_nature_of_suit.formula: share = 100 × cases in the category ÷ all civil cases filed in the district that year, rounded to 1 decimal

criminal_disposition.basis: Criminal defendants whose cases closed in the fiscal year (excluding transfers to another district), by the disposition of the most serious charge, grouped as in the AO's Judicial Business Table D-4.
criminal_disposition.definitions: Guilty pleas include pleas of no contest. Dismissed includes dismissals with or without prejudice, nolle prosequi, pretrial diversion, mistrials and statistical closings. A bench trial is decided by a judge, a jury trial by a jury.
criminal_disposition.formula: share = 100 × defendants whose cases ended this way ÷ all defendants whose cases closed in the district that year, rounded to 1 decimal

groups.label: Not convicted: acquitted by a jury
Not convicted: acquitted by a judge
Not convicted: acquitted by a jury
Not convicted: acquitted by a judge

criminal_offense.basis: Criminal defendants filed in the fiscal year (all offense levels, excluding transfers), grouped by the most serious filing charge into the AO's top-level offense headings.
criminal_offense.formula: share = 100 × defendants in the category ÷ all defendants filed in the district that year, rounded to 1 decimal

groups.label: General offenses (bribery, money laundering, racketeering, extortion, gambling, other)
Property offenses other than fraud (larceny, embezzlement, burglary, forgery, auto theft)
Justice system offenses (escape, obstruction, perjury, contempt)

sentenced_offense.basis: People sentenced in the fiscal year whose primary offense type is known, by the USSC's offense type. Since FY 2018 the USSC assigns the type from the main sentencing guideline applied.
sentenced_offense.definitions: Shares are as the USSC publishes them, so they may not add to exactly 100. They count people sentenced, not charges filed, so they can differ from the criminal charge mix above. "All other offense types" combines the remaining USSC types, which the USSC lists one by one.

groups.formula: 100 × people whose primary offense falls in any other USSC offense type ÷ people sentenced with a known primary offense type (the USSC lists these types separately; the atlas combines them)
groups.label: All other offense types

sentenced_offense.source: U.S. Sentencing Commission, individual offender datafiles

sentencing_composition.note: The USSC changed its sentence categories in FY 2018. The two series are kept apart. Where they overlap (FY 2014 to 2017) the four shares are identical for every district under both schemes. Shares may not add to exactly 100 because each is rounded to one decimal.

context.text: The U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio is one of 9 district courts in the Sixth Circuit. In FY 2025, it had 8 authorized judgeships.

distinctive.method: Generated by a fixed template from the district's outlier statistics: measures where it ranks in the top or bottom three of all districts with data in the latest year, or is the single highest or lowest in its circuit. Zero values, values shared by more than two districts, cells with a data note and shares or medians based on fewer than 50 cases are skipped. No language model is used.
distinctive.paragraph: In FY 2025, 65.8% of pending civil cases had been open for more than three years, the second-highest share of 94 districts. That year, the court had 3,504 pending cases per judgeship, the second-most of 94 districts.

sentences.text: In FY 2025, 65.8% of pending civil cases had been open for more than three years, the second-highest share of 94 districts.

mdl_context.formula: share = 100 × civil cases carrying the MDL docket number ÷ all civil cases filed (or closed) in the district that fiscal year, counted from FJC case records; a note appears when one docket is above 25%
mdl_context.intro: In each year listed here, a single multidistrict litigation (MDL) docket made up more than a quarter of the civil cases this court received or closed.
mdl_context.rule: Shown when one MDL docket made up more than 25% of the court's civil cases filed or closed in a fiscal year from FY 2010 to FY 2026 (preliminary), counted from FJC case records. Those records carry MDL docket numbers for cases closed from FY 2010 on, so earlier years are not checked. A docket is named only when a court record on GovInfo confirms the name; otherwise it is shown by number.
